rationale: A dried-fig trial measured menstrual symptoms and perceived stress. A separate case documented recurrent high potassium after dried figs without a visual hallucination outcome. The recovered Parkinson surgery series reports two postoperative hallucination events. No dried-fig study supplies visual hallucination frequency in Parkinson disease.

A child developed immediate drooling during a fresh-fig allergic reaction. Fig-and-almond syrup and an almond–raisin comparator had similar drooling counts in children receiving methylphenidate. The Parkinson surgery series describes less drooling in two patients who continued infusion. The effect of raw figs on Parkinson drooling severity remains uncertain.

The exact publication audit resolved 27 shared-DOI hits as chronological references or general pain material. The recovered Parkinson surgery series reports qualitative off-period pain changes during surgical and medication care. Primary search trails remain open for dried date and Parkinson pain severity.
